territorial_scope.description: Applies to the Forze di polizia and to civil and criminal proceedings under Italian law.

evidence.quote: Il presente titolo reca disposizioni in materia di utilizzo di sistemi di intelligenza artificiale da parte degli organi, uffici e comandi delle Forze di Polizia

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Legislative decree no. 160 of 9 September 2026 adapts Italian law to the EU AI Act for police use of AI systems and adds AI-related criminal and civil liability rules for AI systems. Police use is governed by its Title I, criminal and civil liability by its Title II.
summary.long: Legislative decree no. 160 of 9 September 2026 adapts Italian law to the EU AI Act for police use of AI systems and adds AI-related criminal and civil liability rules. Title I sets general principles and definitions (Arts 1-2), human review of automated results before use in acts affecting individuals (Art. 3), research collaborations (Art. 4), sandboxes (Art. 5) and training (Art. 6). Chapter III covers biometric uses: labelling and categorisation under conditions (Art. 7); real-time remote biometric identification authorised by a judge for up to fifteen days, with an impact assessment and notification to the Garante (Arts 8-9); post-hoc facial recognition with 48-hour judicial authorisation and a ban on untargeted use (Art. 10). Title II creates criminal offences for omitting safety or human-oversight measures for high-risk AI or altering such systems (Art. 12), allows judicial authorisation of biometric identification of suspects (Art. 13), sets entity sanctions under Decree 231 (Art. 15), and provides civil jurisdiction rules, court-ordered disclosure of evidence (Art. 17), a presumption of causation for AI Act breaches (Art. 18) and direct action against liability insurers (Art. 20). Police AI systems in use at entry into force must be made compliant within one year (Art. 21).

notes: Text is the adopted Decreto legislativo 9 settembre 2026, n. 160 (Normattiva export, ref. 26G00179). The registry title's label AG 418 is a bill reference; the annotation follows the document. The text contains no entry-into-force article; Art. 21 refers to the entry into force date without stating it. Art. 2(1)(p) cites regolamento (UE) 1689/2024 instead of 2024/1689 (apparent citation error). Art. 15(2) inserts a corporate liability offence referring to art. 612-quater c.p., which this text does not amend or introduce. Art. 5(1) states a legal basis for processing that also cites d.lgs. 51/2018. The relations section is populated, so section_status.relations is set to not_applicable only because the schema requires that field; the relations are listed in the relations array.

thresholds.variable_text: maximum statutory penalty of the offence (pena della reclusione nel massimo) for Annex II offences that permit AI real-time remote biometric identification
thresholds.value_text: puniti con la pena della reclusione non inferiore nel massimo a quattro anni
thresholds.measurement: Maximum imprisonment prescribed for the offence by law (nel massimo); applied per offence named in Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
thresholds.consequence: Use of AI systems for real-time remote biometric identification may be authorised, for confirming identity or searching for a person, only where the suspected offence meets this penalty ceiling and is listed in Annex II.
thresholds.conditions: Offence listed in Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; sufficient indicia of commission of the offence (sufficienti indizi); authorisation by the public prosecutor and the judge for preliminary investigations under the procedure in paragraphs 5 to 7.

evidence.quote: puniti con la pena della reclusione non inferiore nel massimo a quattro anni
